title: The Effect of Load and Volume Autoregulation on Muscular Strength and Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
population: 15 studies in resistance-trained individuals: 6 on load autoregulation and 9 on volume autoregulation by velocity loss.
key_findings: Autoregulated load prescription (RIR-based RPE or velocity-based) and fixed percentage-based prescription gave similar 1RM gains.
With sets and relative intensity equated, velocity-loss thresholds of 25% or less gave more 1RM strength but less hypertrophy than thresholds above 25%.
Thresholds above 25% gave more hypertrophy than 20% or less, but no difference was found against 20 to 25%.
methods: Systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA, prospectively registered (PROSPERO CRD42021240506); mean differences and standardized mean differences.
limitations: Few studies per comparison; velocity-loss thresholds change how many repetitions are done, so they mix effort with volume.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
